title: Bridge protocol for vector paging and unified HTTP errors
creator: Maya Alvarez
description: Problem: Multiple customers and older clients rely on differing behaviors from our embeddings and rerank endpoints. Differences include cursor vs offset paging semantics, inconsistent mapping of transient errors (rate limit, capacity throttles) to HTTP status codes, and incompatibilities when clients attempt to resume iteration across failures. This ticket defines and drives a compatibility bridge (proxy) that normalizes paging semantics and error codes so legacy clients see stable behavior while we evolve streaming and structured outputs on the canonical endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility proxy that translates existing legacy client paging patterns (offset+limit, Link header cursors, and opaque cursor tokens) to the canonical cursor model deployed by upstream endpoints

Error normalization layer maps transient internal errors to stable, documented HTTP semantics (e.g., 429 with Retry-After for rate-limit, 503 for capacity, 500+ for internal non-retryable failures) and surfaces structured retry hints in response headers
Preserves idempotency guarantees for rerank requests: retried requests with the same client-provided idempotency token must not double-charge or double-index
Automated test suite with 95%+ coverage for page-boundary edge cases and simulated failure/retry sequences
Canary rollout plan with metrics dashboard: request success rate, cursor-stability rate, client-visible error-change telemetry, and latency P95 for proxied calls
discussion: 2025-02-19 PM sync: raised issue after Support case #S-8840 where two customers saw duplicate items when resuming a paged rerank after a 502. Action: investigate normalization of tombstoning and stable cursors.

2025-02-21 Eng review (Kofi, Sanaa): prototype proxy that accepts legacy 'page' & 'per_page' and emits canonical cursor in body and Link header; concern about added latency from proxy - agreed to keep proxy in the same VPC as runtime and implement fast-path passthrough when client uses canonical contract.
2025-02-24 Security/Compliance: audit of headers confirmed no PII leaked by opaque cursor tokens. Recommended tokens be HMAC-signed and short-lived (24h).

2025-02-27 Runtime team: warned about KV-cache implications for resumed sequences. Decided to include sequence-checksum in cursor to detect model rollout reshuffles and return a 409 with migration hint when sequence mismatch occurs.
2025-03-03 PM review: added acceptance criteria for idempotency token handling per legal and billing requirements.
decisions: Adopt canonical cursor model as single source of truth. The bridge will support legacy offsets/pages by materializing an initial cursor mapping and storing a small, short-lived index in the proxy (TTL 6 hours) to translate offsets to cursor tokens.

Normalize error codes: map internal rate-limit signals to 429 + Retry-After; map capacity-based rejection to 503 with 'X-Redwood-Capacity-Tier' and backoff hints; convert transient 502/504 to 502 with 'Retry-After' for clients that rely on immediate retry semantics.

Expose structured retry hints via 'X-Redwood-Retry' header containing a comma-separated hint set (e.g., 'backoff=linear;min=2;max=30'). This is a temporary, documented bridge field for legacy clients.

Opaque cursors must be HMAC-signed and include a sequence checksum. If checksum mismatch, return 409 and include 'migration_playbook' link in response body for clients to follow graceful fallback steps.
Performance target for proxy added latency: median +1ms, P95 +10ms. If cannot meet, we'll explore in-line adapters in runtime to avoid hop.
Canary to start at 1% of traffic for 72 hours, then 10% for 7 days before full rollout.
tasks: ENG: Build compatibility-proxy service (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/compat-proxy) with translation layers for paging and errors
ENG: Implement HMAC cursor format + sequence checksum generator in runtime and proxy
ENG: Add comprehensive integration tests simulating client resume after 502/502 and verifying no duplicates
PM: Draft public compatibility Playbook and migration FAQ (Confluence link) for customers
DX: Update SDKs (python/node) to prefer canonical cursor but include legacy adapter shims
SRE: Add dashboards for 'cursor-stability-rate', 'compat-proxy-latency', 'client-visible-error-delta' and alert rules if error-delta > 5%
PM: Coordinate canary cohorts and outreach to top-10 affected customers to observe behavior
notes: Risk: proxy state for offset->cursor materialization imposes extra memory; capped TTL to 6 hours and soft eviction policy recommended.
Trade-off: We could instead force all clients to move to canonical cursor immediately but customer fallout and onboarding cost is high. Bridge approach chosen to reduce churn.
Follow-up: after stable rollouts, evaluate deprecation timeline for legacy offset API (proposed 12-18 months post-rollout).
